title: I built a feed where one typed sentence becomes a playable web game
author: Less-Review9327
selftext:
BBOX started as a feed of short browser games. The part I finished recently: type one sentence in the app and it generates a playable HTML5 game from that prompt — no engine, no code, no asset pipeline — then publishes it straight into the feed.

The clip is one of those games. Everything on screen came from the prompt, including the look.

Curious whether this reads as "AI generated a game" or "AI generated a prototype" to people here — that gap is the interesting part for me.

iOS: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bbox/id6785750266
Web: https://bbox.games/play

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: Make games like with Claude but upload instantly so people can swipe, play, comment, and compete on the leaderboard.

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: And the games will be better quality than Claude’s.

replies.author: Mezezius
replies.body: how can it make better games than Claude when it is just Claude lmao

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: Then just ask an AI once to make a plane game and see if the quality actually comes out good.

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: Because it runs on top of the pipeline and harness I built, you can get better results.

replies.author: Comet7777
replies.body: Claude now allows you to turn your prompt into an app. They could decide tomorrow to do that for games and it becomes the default solution for everyone.

comments.author: DiscountCthulhu01
comments.body: Yeah because the one thing there's a shortage of is ultra bad slop games...

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: If you came and looked, you wouldn’t think the games were that bad quality.

replies.author: DiscountCthulhu01
replies.body:
"The clip is one of those games. Everything on screen came from the prompt, including the look."

I am 100% sure this is your best foot forward, which does anything but inspire confidence...

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: I only included that game because it was easy to understand intuitively. It's by no means my best work. In fact, it's closer to being my worst game than my best.

replies.author: plazebology
replies.body: Show us your best or come to terms with the fact that what you’ve shown us looks like garbage and so people will assume it’s garbage; that‘s on you

replies.author: DiscountCthulhu01
replies.body: None of it is your work though,  right? :D cmon man

comments.author: plazebology
comments.body: Why are yall so obsessed with disposable media

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: You can also make games yourself and upload them. Same as Reels — some people post whatever, and some put real care into it.

replies.author: plazebology
replies.body: Cool, not really an answer to my question

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: Here you can try games instantly and save the ones you like. so it’s less disposable media and more a faster way to find games you’d enjoy than hunting on the App Store. You don’t have to download anything just to see if it’s fun, and recommendations surface games you’re likely to like.

replies.author: plazebology
replies.body: This is definitely disposable media. What do you think happens to the games you don't like? Can we go back to designing stuff based on efficiency instead of novelty for the sake of novelty?

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: We should celebrate that we’re past the era where creativity from people who don’t code just got wasted. And on the App Store you bounce after a screenshot and a blurb — on BBOX you actually play it and see if it fits you. What’s the problem?

replies.author: plazebology
replies.body:
Let me translate:

„Disposable media is better!“ 

You have no sense of scarcity of resources and are participating in a market you know absolutely nothing about, probably because Claude told you to

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
That makes a great intro for a Black Mirror episode, watching young people going from one slop game to another because each game had no long-term engagement and becomes quickly boring - and eventually they have the attention span of a goldfish, only consuming slop day-in day-out.

Seriously, the lengths engineerswould  go to do anything but actually design games. I perceive this as a general trend, people with technical skills that want to make games but have no intention to put in the work into designing one.

replies.author: Less-Review9327
replies.body: I agree that designing games matters. But a game isn’t only a game after years of polishing. if the balance works, almost any idea can be fun. What matters is creativity. People who had ideas locked away because they couldn’t code can finally turn those creative games into something real

replies.author: plazebology
replies.body: People like you act like devs are born with the skills, time and effort it takes to make a good game
